questions.problem: Suppose that the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{3}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{3}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1},\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the two given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{7}{R}_{3}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{7}{R}_{3}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{7}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{7} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{7} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$
